For example in Japan, you pay for most things in cash. People have cash in their wallets and rarely use a card (well, that was my experience when visiting relatives). In America however, many people use credit and debit cards to pay for everything, even daily things such as groceries.

Which do you believe is better? To keep a steady amount of cash available at hand or leave it all in a bank, with a debit card instead?
Is it better to keep cash or a debit card on hand?

I keep some cash and some cards. I don't use a debit card as it doesn't have the same protection as a credit card. Generally I use a card for gas, groceries, and pretty much anything over $10 or $20. I usually keep about $100 or so in cash in my wallet.

I also keep about 6 months of expenses in cash, as well as about 6 months of expenses in the bank accessible by card if necessary. This enables me to deal with typically any kind of disaster such as a run on the bank, or if cash becomes a problem, such as they are having in India ATM.

I say card for convenience. I keep a small amount of cash at all times, but do most of my payments by card.

I use separate accounts for different budget items. One for groceries, one for "other" and one for disposable personal. Each account gets an automatic transfer on the first of the month with the designated amount. I keep track of how the account drops over the month so no category goes over budget.

As long as you're not using a credit card for things like groceries, you're OK. I think that is a big mistake, it likely means you have no idea how much you spend on groceries.

When I was in Uni I used a credit card at the grocery store. I felt like I didn't need to go to the food bank because wasn't poor enough for a place like that. Hahaahaha. Then came the time to pay back student loans, and yeah, pretty much all of my food came from the food bank. Most of the food I bought with the credit card was stuff I later got from the food bank anyways (think Ramen, cans of pasta sauce, etc.)

I usually keep 40-80 hard cash in my wallet and use it for most purchases. I use my debit card at grocery stores and stores that are unlikely to have their card reader compromised. I use my credit card for most other things and pay of the balance every month. With a credit card its easier to get reimbursed for fraudulent charges. I'm cheap as fuck and can usually get by with 60 in cash I get at the grocery store when I do my shopping every two weeks.
Keep cash on you if you're traveling / road trip, otherwise normal daily routine just use debit.
